headline: Pakistan vows to defend Saudi Arabia to any extent amid Houthi attacks
summary: Pakistan's military spokesman says the country will provide both diplomatic and physical support to the kingdom as tensions rise in the region.
details: Pakistan's military spokesman, Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, stated that his country will "go to any extent" to defend Saudi Arabia, following increased attacks from Yemen's Houthi forces.
The commitment comes as Riyadh accused Houthi rebels of launching a "cowardly" attack targeting the holy city of Mecca, which sparked widespread outrage across the Muslim world.
In an interview with Arab News, Chaudhry emphasized that Pakistan would back the kingdom both diplomatically and physically, specifically for the security of the two holy sanctuaries.
This pledge follows the signing of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement last month between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey, committing the three nations to mutual defence if any of them are attacked.
The regional tension is further heightened by the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran, as well as attacks from Tehran-backed Houthi rebels.
caption:
Pakistan will "go to any extent" to defend Saudi Arabia.

Diplomatic and physical support promised amid rising Houthi attacks.

Pakistan's military spokesman, Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, stated that his country will "go to any extent" to defend Saudi Arabia, following increased attacks from Yemen's Houthi forces.

The commitment comes as Riyadh accused Houthi rebels of launching a "cowardly" attack targeting the holy city of Mecca, which sparked widespread outrage across the Muslim world.

In an interview with Arab News, Chaudhry emphasized that Pakistan would back the kingdom both diplomatically and physically, specifically for the security of the two holy sanctuaries.

This pledge follows the signing of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement last month between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey, committing the three nations to mutual defence if any of them are attacked.

The regional tension is further heightened by the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran, as well as attacks from Tehran-backed Houthi rebels.

topic: Bhutan PM makes brief stopover in Dhaka
headline_marked: Bhutan PM Tshering Tobgay makes [[brief stopover in Dhaka]]
headline: Bhutan PM Tshering Tobgay makes brief stopover in Dhaka
summary: The Prime Minister of Bhutan arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Friday for a short transit before heading to Germany.
details: Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Friday, September 18, at 1:55 PM.
During his brief transit, he was welcomed by Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives (LGRD) Minister Dr. Abdul Moin Khan and State Minister for Foreign Affairs-1 Humayun Kabir.
The Prime Minister's stopover in the capital lasted approximately 45 minutes.
Following the formalities at the airport, he departed from Dhaka on a chartered flight bound for Germany.
caption:
Bhutan's Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay touched down in Dhaka for a quick 45-minute transit stop.

Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Friday, September 18, at 1:55 PM.

During his brief transit, he was welcomed by Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives (LGRD) Minister Dr. Abdul Moin Khan and State Minister for Foreign Affairs-1 Humayun Kabir.

The Prime Minister's stopover in the capital lasted approximately 45 minutes.

Following the formalities at the airport, he departed from Dhaka on a chartered flight bound for Germany.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV
